lines.say: Both atheists and believers love to quote Einstein. So what did he actually say about God?
Famous line, from 1926: God does not play dice. But that was about quantum physics, not religion.

In 1929 a rabbi asked him by telegram if he believed in God. He answered: I believe in Spinoza's God, who reveals himself in the harmony of what exists, not in a God who concerns himself with the fates of human beings.
In 1954 he called the word God an expression of human weakness. That letter later sold for nearly three million dollars.
But he also refused to be called an atheist. He said he felt awe at the structure of the universe, and called that feeling religious.
So: no personal God who answers prayers. But not no God at all. Something closer to the order of nature itself.
